justification: New scripts/derive_precinct_keys.py: a config-driven, idempotent precinct-keying DERIVATION pass. Root-cause fix for the year-long churn (docs/EXTRACTION_WHY_IT_RECURS_AND_THE_DURABLE_FIX_2026-07.md): v2_precinct_id was applied by hand, so every re-extraction nulled it and the manual re-key recurred. This derives the key from a written rule per (council,chapter) so re-running reproduces it and re-extraction stops being destructive. Default dry-run; --apply gated + backup; only writes rows whose derived key differs; never touches provision_text. A derived key also sets v2_dcp_layer='precinct' (a keyed row is a precinct-layer row).

pre_impl.existing_data: Keying strategies were worked out and applied MANUALLY across this session (Marrickville doc-suffix->N_, Leichhardt C2 ref-regex, Ashfield E2 whole-doc->Haberfield, KG single-site constants, Ashfield ch-D page-range). ACCEPTANCE TEST run: --validate against the live DB REPRODUCES the existing manual keys exactly — Marrickville 1456/1456, Leichhardt 867/867, Ashfield-E2 118/120 already-ok (2 non-actionable). Ashfield ch-D deliberately validate:False (its rows were hand-patched via text-location+duplication, not page — 302 would-change; the page rule is going-forward-correct, applied only after a clean re-extraction).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: If a chapter's real keying isn't expressible by one of the 5 strategies, the rule returns None for those rows (reported as no-derivation) and leaves them untouched — never guesses.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Backend derivation, inverse of the frontend precinct-serving code (precinct-service.ts reads the key; this writes it). No prior backend keyer existed.

functions.name: _derive
functions.input: a strategy dict + a provision row dict (document_id/ref_number/pdf_page/source_chapter_key)
functions.output: the derived v2_precinct_id string, or None when the strategy does not match the row
functions.if_none: row is counted no-derivation and left untouched — the pass never writes a guessed key

functions.name: run
functions.input: council filter, apply bool, validate bool; reads current rows per RULES selector
functions.output: per-rule new/changed/already-ok/no-derivation counts; on --apply, guarded UPDATE of v2_precinct_id + layer with CSV backup
functions.if_none: dry-run (default) writes nothing; --validate rolls back and exits 1 if any validate-rule's derived key disagrees with the existing key

values.value: 5 rules: marrickville_part9 (doc_regex), leichhardt_c2 (ref_regex), ashfield_e2 (constant Haberfield), ku_ring_gai_part14_single_site (chapter_map), ashfield_chapter_d_parts (page_range, validate:False)
values.if_missing: a council with no rule is simply not processed — no rows touched

queries.purpose: select current rows a rule targets
queries.where_clause: WHERE is_current = true AND source_council = %(council)s AND (<rule.where>)

queries.purpose: apply the derived key (only when different)
queries.where_clause: UPDATE ... SET v2_precinct_id=%s, v2_dcp_layer='precinct' WHERE id=%s

break_it.scenario: The page-range rule for Ashfield ch-D is applied and overwrites the more-accurate hand-patched (text-location + per-part-duplication) keys.
break_it.what_happens: 302 rows would change to page-derived keys, regressing the duplication handling.
break_it.how: validate:False keeps it out of --validate; and it only runs when --council ashfield is passed. The doc directs: apply page rule ONLY after a clean columnar re-extraction, not against the current patchwork.
break_it.repro: python scripts/derive_precinct_keys.py --council ashfield (dry-run shows 302 changed — do not --apply)

break_it.scenario: A rule's regex matches a row it shouldn't and derives a wrong key.
break_it.what_happens: A wrong v2_precinct_id would be written to that provision row, mis-keying it.
break_it.how: --validate asserts every derived key on a validate-rule reproduces the human-verified existing key (2441 real rows reproduced exactly); unit tests pin each strategy incl. non-match->None.

break_it.scenario: The --apply pass is run a second time against the same already-keyed rows.
break_it.how: idempotent: rows already keyed correctly count already-ok and are skipped (only writes where derived != current or layer != precinct).
break_it.repro: run --apply twice; second shows new=0 changed=0

post_merge.db_reset: Not required — pass is opt-in per council.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - after --council ku_ring_gai --apply, the KG single-site boundaries (14I/14J/14K/14L) connect and those addresses serve their precinct rules.
